lesson.summary: Introduction to C: History, Characteristics and Classification
points: Dennis Ritchie developed C at Bell Labs in the early 1970s, building on B in the Unix environment.
C is general purpose, procedural and imperative; it is normally compiled.
Portability needs care with implementation-dependent behavior. Middle-level is an informal classroom label, not an ISO language category.

archive_evidence.history: Ritchie wrote the first compiler for C while developing the language from B at Bell Labs.
archive_evidence.source: Dennis Ritchie, The Development of the C Language

archive_evidence.history: Herman Hollerith's machine-readable cards helped the United States process its census data mechanically.
Dennis Ritchie developed C at Bell Laboratories. He wrote its first compiler and refined the language alongside the Unix project.
archive_evidence.source: Dennis Ritchie, The Development of the C Language

archive_evidence.history: Ken Thompson developed B. Ritchie developed C from it. Many Bell Labs colleagues contributed tools and language ideas.
archive_evidence.source: Dennis Ritchie, The Development of the C Language

archive_evidence.history: Brian Kernighan and Dennis Ritchie coauthored a book that helped teach and document C. The book appeared after the language was already in use.
archive_evidence.source: Dennis Ritchie, The Development of the C Language
